source.comparison: User-supplied highstreet.png, 2026-09-26; underlying OS map date not independently established from that screenshot. Geometry uses the archived NLS layer in the factory coordinate frame.

policy: Main building ranges, not occupied land parcels. Use is unassigned unless explicitly labelled on the map. Two-storey elevations and divisions are estimates; no invented shop signs or tenants. Existing factory and housing footprints take precedence at registration overlaps.

buildings.evidence: Main envelope read from OS; exact rear additions, storeys, facade and occupancy unresolved.

osRegistration.osReading: On the OS five-foot plan (1893 sheets, NLS mosaic) and the EPFL 1891-96 footprints traced from it, the printed south-east building line here stands 8.41 m (median of 72 perpendicular readings every 0.25 m along the range) from the retraced High Street centreline; fitted line residual at most 0.14 m. EPFL footprint cover of the new plan 0.92, of the prior plan 0.09.
osRegistration.interpretation: The prior plan put the street face -0.85/-0.59 m from the centreline, in the carriageway. Moved 9.33 m (dx 7.29, dz 5.83) so the street face lies on the printed building line (8.33/8.44 m); south-west end shortened 4.2 m (width 23.65 -> 19.45 m) because the OS steps the building line back 2.4 m there (readings 10.8-11.0 m) behind a small projecting porch or bay (6.9 m); the prior range ran across that forecourt; rotation -38.17 -> -38.47 degrees to follow that line. Depth 10.03 m, storeys, height and roof unchanged; width 19.45 m.

buildings.name: Marshgate corner public house
buildings.evidence: Main envelope read from OS; exact rear additions, storeys, facade and occupancy unresolved.

osRegistration.osReading: The OS five-foot plan prints the P.H. as one shaded block on the south-west side of Marshgate Lane at its High Street corner (EPFL footprint sourceFid 91288, 108 m2): lane face from (-835.6, -83.3) to (-828.7, -74.6) with a chamfer to the High Street, about 13.3-13.9 m along the lane and 10.2 m across, with a notch on its south-west side. The printed lane between this face and the block opposite (EPFL sourceFid 24982, 213 m2) is about 6.2 m wide. The prior plan stood 7 m north-west of the P.H. and 6-7 m into the lane, over open roadway (EPFL cover 0.32).
osRegistration.interpretation: Re-registered onto the printed P.H. block: moved 10.16 m (dx -0.32, dz 10.15); width across the lane 9.5 m kept; length along the lane 11.1 -> 13.3 m because the OS prints one block of that length. EPFL cover of the new plan 0.81. The modelled Marshgate Lane is itself about 3 m west of the printed lane here (its centreline runs 0.2 m from the P.H. face), so the builder trims the lane side of this range; the lane, not the range, is wrong for that remaining clash.
osRegistration.laneMisregistration: Marshgate Lane centreline between (-828.8, -74.5) and (-842.1, -99.4) lies about 3 m west of the printed lane centre; left for a road retrace.

vista.photo: reference/Images and Figures/PossibleCover_Three Mills Wall London Fireworks Co 1900.jpg
vista.photoDate: circa 1900, supplied filename; original archive date not independently verified
vista.orientation: Working south-facing view from the High Street end, east bank on the left; exact camera remains provisional
observed: Narrow unsurfaced path above the water on the left
Close boarded boundary fence and lower riverside timber rail
Grassy bank face with a timber-retained toe
Two-storey brick premises on the left and waterside masonry on the right
Tall gabled warehouse in the distance
vista.interpretation: The existing Sugar House is a candidate for the distant warehouse. Its identification and the exact camera need further photographic fitting. The photo establishes types and relative arrangement, not surveyed metric dimensions.
vista.limits: Path dimensions, heights, individual tree positions, timber details and all absolute offsets are photo-informed estimates attached to the existing GIS bank. No 1930s concrete embankment geometry is introduced. No photographic texture is used.

connections.evidence: Interpreted bank access to Abbey Lane/High Street, reconciled with GIS bank and provisional frontage placement; not a surveyed route.
OS five-foot map shows continuous east-bank route. Intermediate alignment follows GIS shore; junction and levels interpreted.
OS east-bank lane continues to the distillery approach; connection geometry and level inferred.
